summary: The implementation does what PLAN.md rev 2.3 §4/§5/§6 says, nothing beyond the user's decisions moved, the tests discriminate as claimed, and the paid acceptance proves the narquil repair. It is ready to commit after the fixes below. One finding is substantive and goes to the user (F1): a `fun`/`function` declared inside a theory-level `context fixes x … begin … end` block whose equations use `x` is stored in the function package's registry under the compound key `f ?x` (the block's fixed variable becomes a parameter when the definition is exported to the theory), and the code's bare-constant query cannot reach a compound key, so for that ordinary shape the digest stays body-free — the same silent staleness acceptance_step10 finding 1 reported — and neither PLAN §7 nor limitation #8 records it. I verified every link of that chain in the Isabelle2025-2 sources and found two shipped instances (HOL-Library/Power_By_Squaring.thy, HOL-IMP/Collecting.thy) outside the heap the census enumerated. It needs one REPL probe and a user choice between a small code extension (query every application depth up to the arity; plus a new test S13i and plan wording) and documenting it as a fourth surviving shape. Everything else is implementer's-call material: one false cause in a test comment (the `_def_raw` note, found by three lenses), `prop_ord` bound below the two long comments that explain `spec_rule_axioms`, two factual slips in ACCEPTANCE.md (three new-key facts counted as enrolment evidence; `galmuth_dom` listed as a walled dependent though it has no edge to `galmuth`), and four doc sentences (limitation #8 asserts morphism-transformed registry keys the census did not find; §7.3 item 1 defends the registry branch with a refutable clause; §3.2's cross-reference is stale; the §14 change-2 row puts the desired behaviour in the failure column, contrary to PLAN §5/§8). The nitpick filters were right on every rejection except F5, which is the same defect as R4-1. Not part of this object and must stay out of the commit, as the HANDOFF already says: the foreign edits to Tools/entity_position.ML (a TEMPORARY hunt marker) and archive/tests/test_migrate_from_collection.py.

rulings.title: A `fun` under theory-level `context fixes x` with `x` in its equations is keyed `f ?x` in the registry; the bare-constant query never reaches it, so the repaired defect survives for that shape, undocumented
rulings.location: /home/qiyuan/Current/MLML/contrib/Semantic_Embedding/Tools/semantic_digest.ML:358-372 (function_equations, the query `Const (const_name, T)`); ai-artifacts/fun_digest/PLAN.md §2 ("hence a bare Const only when no term-rewriting mixin intervened"), §4 lookup note, §7; doc/invalidation_limitations.md #8 (:300-327)
rulings.reasoning: Confirmed by reading the sources (not measured in Isabelle, which this review may not do). What happens, step by step: inside `context fixes k :: nat begin fun step … end`, the function package defines `step` with `Local_Theory.define`; `Generic_Target.define` (generic_target.ML:254-289) finds `k` in the expanded right-hand side, makes it a parameter, so the theory-level constant is `T.step :: nat ⇒ nat ⇒ nat` with foundation `step k ≡ step_sumC k`, and returns the local `Free step`; `Mutual.define_projections` stores that `Free` as the function term and `mk_partial_rules_mutual` (mutual.ML:274-278) builds `fs` from it. The registry declaration (function.ML:135-136, :213-216) is non-pervasive; an unnamed context block reuses the theory target's operations (local_theory.ML:443-448, named_target.ML:99), so it runs `Generic_Target.theory_declaration` → `background_declaration` → `Local_Theory.standard_form`, whose morphism starts with `Proof_Context.export_morphism` = `Assumption.export_morphism $> Variable.export_morphism`: the local definition is expanded (`Free step` → `Const T.step $ Free k`, local_defs.ML:98-100) and the block-fixed `k` is generalised to a schematic variable (variable.ML:516-531, :574-583). So the theory-level registry key is `T.step ?k`. The net keys it `[CombK, AtomK T.step, VarK]` (net.ML:53-62); for a `Const` query `matching` calls `rands t (net, var::nets)` → `look1 (atoms, c)`, i.e. only bare-atom keys plus the root wildcard branch, never the `comb` subnet (net.ML:193-208). The constant's Defs axiom `T.step_def` is own-theory and body-free, so rule ③ fires, `function_equations` returns `[]`, and the digest never sees an equation edit — acceptance_step10 finding 1 again, on that shape. Shipped instances: HOL-Library/Power_By_Squaring.thy:14-24 (`context fixes f … function efficient_funpow`, `f` in the equations) and HOL-IMP/Collecting.thy:17-26 (`context fixes f g … fun Step`); both lie outside the 87-theory Semantic_Embedding heap the census walked, which is exactly why CENSUS (g) saw only bare keys and why this is a real gap the plan did not measure. Neither PLAN §7 nor limitation #8 lists the shape. Not a settled decision: F3 fixes the SOURCE (the registry), F7 makes details the implementer's, but the query term was reviewed three rounds as `Const (c, T)`, extending it changes which digests move, and there are two reasonable code shapes — so the user decides. The Var-headed wildcard query the census used is NOT an option for production: it returns the whole registry and `retrieve_function_data` runs `transform_function_data` on every returned entry (function_common.ML:279-281), so each constant query would cost the registry's size.
rulings.fix: Step (i), first, through the REPL server only (no isabelle build): a 10-line probe theory `theory P imports Main begin context fixes k :: nat begin fun step :: "nat ⇒ nat" where "step 0 = k" | "step (Suc n) = step n + k" end end`; print the registry's keys with the CENSUS (g) wildcard query and `Semantic_Digest.own_defining_axioms` for `P.step`. Expected: key `step ?k`; props today only `P.step_def`. If the probe refutes this, close the finding with the probe output. If confirmed, the user chooses: OPTION A (recommended, code): in `function_equations` replace the single query by one per application depth 0..arity — `val arity = length (binder_types T); fun query n = Function_Common.retrieve_function_data (#ctxt env) (list_comb (Const (const_name, T), map (fn i => Var (("a", i), dummyT)) (1 upto n)))` and `maps query (0 upto arity) |> filter keyed_on_const |> maps (equations o snd) |> sort prop_ord`. A `Var` argument is a wildcard for the net (`net_skip`, net.ML:198-203), a depth-n query returns exactly the entries keyed with n arguments (depth-0 the bare key, so no entry comes back twice), `dummyT` is fine because the net ignores types, and `keyed_on_const` keeps doing its root-wildcard job. Add one sentence to the block comment: "A `fun` declared under `context fixes x` with `x` in its equations is keyed `f ?x` (the block's fixed variables become parameters on export), so every application depth up to the arity is queried." Test S13i in Test/Test_Sensitivity.thy, subject declared with the S13 subjects (before the ML block that builds env3): `context fixes sens_k :: nat begin fun sens_cfun :: "nat ⇒ nat" where "sens_cfun 0 = sens_k" | "sens_cfun (Suc n) = sens_cfun n + sens_k" end`, asserting `mentions (own "sens_cfun") "Groups.plus_class.plus"` — red today, green after; the type `nat ⇒ nat ⇒ nat` and the body-free Defs axiom cannot supply `plus`. Docs: PLAN §2's clause "hence a bare Const only when no term-rewriting mixin intervened" gains "or when the constant was declared under `context fixes` with the fixed variable in its equations (key `f ?x`; distribution instances Power_By_Squaring.efficient_funpow, IMP.Collecting.Step)"; PLAN §4's lookup note states the per-depth query. Then a short re-review of the code change. Alternative code shape for the record (more principled, slightly bigger): query with the left-hand side of each own-theory Defs axiom (`fst (Logic.dest_equals (Logic.strip_imp_concl prop))`), which is by construction the same `list_comb (Const f, params)` the registry keyed; it needs `distinct` on the answer because an `overloading` family's several bare-lhs axioms (CENSUS (d), `sz`) would return the one entry several times. OPTION B (documentation only): a fourth bullet in PLAN §7 and a fourth shape in limitation #8 (with the two distribution instances), so the gap is at least on record; the code stays as is.

rulings.title: S13g's `_def_raw` note states a false cause: every `definition` writes `c_def_raw` to Defs, argument on the lhs or not
rulings.reasoning: Three lenses found the same thing and I confirmed it: `Specification.gen_def` (Pure/Isar/specification.ML:258-260) has one path — `val name = Thm.def_binding_optional b a` then `Local_Theory.define_internal ((b, mx), ((Binding.suffix_name "_raw" name, []), rhs))` — with no branch on the argument list; the `_def` fact is produced afterwards by `Local_Theory.notes` (:262-264) as a derived theorem and never enters Defs. The module itself cites the argument-free case (`Fun.id_def_raw`, semantic_digest.ML:236). The assertion is right; the sentence explaining it names a condition that does not exist, and the next person adding an argument-free control will write `_def` and go red for a reason unrelated to the branch (the saved red copy at scratchpad/fun_impl/Test_Sensitivity_Red.thy:316 already made that slip).
rulings.fix: Replace the comment line with: `(* \`definition\` always records its Defs axiom as \`_def_raw\` (Specification.gen_def); \`_def\` is the derived fact *)`. No assertion or expected value changes.

rulings.title: ACCEPTANCE.md counts three new-key facts among narquil's re-interpreted lemmas and says all eight were untouched in acceptance_step10
rulings.location: /home/qiyuan/Current/MLML/contrib/Semantic_Embedding/ai-artifacts/fun_digest/ACCEPTANCE.md, section "(iii) The live run: PASS", third PASS bullet
rulings.reasoning: Verified against the raw logs. `narquil.simps(1)` and `narquil.elims` quote the edited equation, so their statements changed between A1 and B and they are NEW statement-keyed entities, answered whatever the digest does: /var/tmp/qiyuan/fun_accept_logs/inspect_after_run2.txt has two rows each (old key 128/128 kept, new key at 132), and host_run2.log answers them at 17:05:30 in the seed batch (:244-246), before narquil's verdict at 17:05:43 (:282). The enrolment evidence is the five same-key records that rose 128 → 132 — `narquil.simps(2)`, `narquil_small`, `narquil_large`, `narquil_glaive_commute`, `narquil_glaive_assoc` — answered at 17:06:25 after the verdict (:324-328). acceptance_step10's own dump (/var/tmp/qiyuan/gate_accept_logs/inspect_after_run2.txt:50-54, :102-103) already shows the same two-row pairs, so "in acceptance_step10 these lemmas were untouched" is false for those three. Cross-check: 23 enrolled here − 18 enrolled in acceptance_step10 (REPORT.md:42) = 5. The PASS verdict stands (PLAN §9 item 3 names the four `narquil_*` lemmas, all among the five); the record's attribution is what is wrong, and the record already draws this exact distinction for `galmuth`.
rulings.fix: Rewrite the bullet: the enrolment evidence is the five same-key records whose `interpreted_at` rose 128 → 132 (`narquil_small`, `narquil_large`, `narquil_glaive_commute`, `narquil_glaive_assoc`, `narquil.simps(2)`; host_run2.log :324-328, after the verdict); `narquil.simps(1)` and `narquil.elims` (kinds 2 and 34) changed statement and were answered in the seed batch as new theorem keys (:244-246), in acceptance_step10 as well, so they are not evidence of the repair; restrict "in acceptance_step10 these lemmas were untouched" to the five; add the cross-check 23 − 18 = 5.

rulings.title: ACCEPTANCE.md lists `galmuth_dom` among the walled dependents, but `galmuth_dom` has no edge to `galmuth`
rulings.reasoning: Verified. `galmuth_dom` is the abbreviation `accp galmuth_rel` the package creates (function_core.ML:890-893). In `sem_constant` (semantic_digest.ML:424-440) an abbreviation's edges come from its rhs (`Wellfounded.accp`, the recordless `galmuth_rel`) plus the type constants; `galmuth` is not among them, so no verdict on `galmuth` could enrol it and its 128/128 says nothing about the wall. The run's own control proves it: `narquil_dom` stays 128/128 beside `narquil` minted to 132 (inspect_after_run2.txt :10-11), while narquil's five real dependents moved. Small, but the list is presented as the set of dependents that were walled, and someone reusing it as galmuth's edge set gets a wrong set.
rulings.fix: Delete `galmuth_dom` from the parenthesised list of walled dependents (leaving the five lemmas). Optionally add: "`galmuth_dom` (the abbreviation `accp galmuth_rel`) has no edge to `galmuth`, as `narquil_dom` staying at 128/128 beside the minted `narquil` shows."

rulings.title: Limitation #8 asserts morphism-transformed registry keys that the census did not find
rulings.location: /home/qiyuan/Current/MLML/contrib/Semantic_Embedding/doc/invalidation_limitations.md #8, first bullet ("登记表里只有经 locale 注册 morphism 变换后的键 …") and the '为何接受' clause "再接一层 locale morphism"
rulings.reasoning: The census enumerated the theory-visible net completely (a Var-headed query takes `net_skip` and returns every leaf) and found 19 entries in HOL.Bit_Operations, none mentioning `fold2_bit_int`, and 0 for each of the three `global_interpretation … defines` constants (CENSUS (b), (g)). So there is no morphism-transformed key in the theory-visible registry at all; why the registrations produce none was not measured. The doc turned PLAN §2's mechanism phrasing into a presence claim, and its remedy sketch then points a future implementer at a key that is not there. PLAN §7 (the authority) states only the measured absence.
rulings.fix: Replace the clause with PLAN §7's measured wording: "theory 可见的登记表里没有任何键提到该 locale 常量或它经 `global_interpretation … defines` 得到的常量（CENSUS (b)：wildcard 枚举 19 条，无一相关），裸常量查询返回 0"; in '为何接受' replace "再接一层 locale morphism" with "另找一条取到方程的路（locale 内部的登记未测）".

rulings.title: §7.3 item 1 defends the registry branch with the refutable clause "方程只能从登记表取到"
rulings.location: /home/qiyuan/Current/MLML/contrib/Semantic_Embedding/archive/plans/CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md §7.3 item 1 (:358-359); the parallel clause "reachable only through the registry" in ai-artifacts/fun_digest/PLAN.md §6
rulings.reasoning: §7.3 exists to stop deletions, and its sentence is refutable as an Isabelle fact: function.ML:217 registers the same `tsimps` in Spec_Rules. The two facts that actually make the branch irreplaceable — which I verified — are: (a) an unterminated `function` has a registry entry with psimps (function.ML:134-136) and no Spec_Rules item at all (CENSUS (a) `pb_vurn`); (b) the Spec_Rules item of a terminated function is added under `Binding.empty`, whose full name is the empty string (binding.ML `name_spec`: empty name → `spec' = []` → `full_name = ""`), and `same_theory` then compares `leading_component ""` = `""` (`space_explode _ "" = []`) against the theory base name and can never pass — so the existing `spec_rule_axioms` cannot return a function's equations however it is gated, and using Spec_Rules for them would need `Spec_Rules.dest_theory` (F4, ruled out). Stating these accurately restates F3/F4/F5 and re-opens nothing.
rulings.fix: In CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN §7.3 item 1 replace "函数包写进 Defs 的公理是 `f ≡ f_sumC`，不含方程体，方程只能从登记表取到" with "函数包写进 Defs 的公理是 `f ≡ f_sumC`，不含方程体；Spec_Rules 里的同一组方程以 `Binding.empty` 登记（`function.ML:217`），无名，`same_theory` 永远过不了（要用它只能 `Spec_Rules.dest_theory`，F4 已否），而未证终止的 `function` 在 Spec_Rules 里根本没有条目、只有登记表有 psimps". In PLAN.md §6 the clause "so the equations are reachable only through the registry" becomes "so the equations are reachable only through the registry: the Spec_Rules item is nameless (`Binding.empty`, function.ML:217) and cannot pass `same_theory`, and an unterminated `function` has no Spec_Rules item at all".

rulings.title: §3.2's constant row still says deps come from a "三层过滤" of defining axioms
rulings.reasoning: Verified: :123 reads "own-defining-axioms 三层过滤（§7.3 详述）提取的定义公理中出现的 …". §7.3 item 1 was retitled "过滤与来源" in this change because a source was added, so the label names a heading that no longer exists, and "定义公理" no longer covers the registry equations (derived theorems, not axioms) — the signature comment at semantic_digest.ML:66-70 makes that distinction, the parent design's one summary sentence does not. The failure scenario is overstated (the cross-reference still lands on the item that explains the new edge), so this is one phrase, not more. §12 step 9's "三层过滤" is the historical step list and stays.

rulings.title: §14 change-2 row puts the desired behaviour into the '缺了会怎样' cell, contrary to PLAN §5/§8
rulings.reasoning: Verified: the row reads "| `digest_term t = Term_Digest.term128 t` | digest 在 hash 前被做了变换（参数改名使 digest 变化——归一化已撤销，2026-09-13） |". The table's second column is what goes wrong without the assertion, and every parenthesis in it gives the cause of the failure; here the parenthesis names the behaviour F6′ WANTS (a rename moving the digest), so a reader scanning that column takes S14 to guard against the opposite of the decision. PLAN §5 puts the rename fact in the first cell and §8 says the row is rewritten as §5 says; keeping the literal assertion in cell 1 is fine under F7, the misplaced fact is the only defect.
rulings.fix: Rewrite the row as "| `digest_term t = Term_Digest.term128 t`（参数改名使 digest 变化） | digest 在 hash 前被做了变换（归一化已撤销，2026-09-13） |".
